name: 2D Texture-Based Volume Rendering
definition: A GPU rendering method where volumetric data is stored in 2D texture images, projected onto the image plane as object-aligned slices, and blended back-to-front.
summary: 2D Texture-Based Volume Rendering is a GPU-accelerated technique that projects volumetric data as stacks of 2D textures onto proxy geometry, distinguishing itself by using bilinear interpolation of 2D slices rather than 3D trilinear sampling.
